bill.title: Providing for congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, of the rule submitted by the Bureau of Land Management relating to Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program Record of Decision.
bill.officialSummary: This joint resolution opens public land for oil and gas leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. Specifically, the joint resolution nullifies the record of decision (ROD) issued by the Bureau of Land Management on December 9, 2024, for the program that leases, develops, produces, and transports oil and gas in and from the Coastal Plain program area within the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. The 2024 ROD that is being nullified by this resolution replaced the 2020 ROD that made all of the approximately 1.6 million acres of the program area available for oil and gas leasing. The 2024 ROD made approximately 1.2 million acres unavailable for leasing or exploration in order to protect and conserve resources and certain uses in these areas. However, the 2024 ROD requires the statutory minimum of 400,000 acres to be made available for oil and gas leasing in a specified lease sale, subject to certain stipulations and operating procedures. Under current law, those acres must be located in the areas with the highest potential for the discovery of hydrocarbons.

classification.plainSummary: This joint resolution would reverse a December 2024 decision by the Bureau of Land Management that restricted oil and gas leasing in Alaska's Arctic National Wildlife Refuge. The 2024 decision made about 1.2 million acres unavailable for leasing while keeping the legally required minimum of 400,000 acres open. If this resolution passes, it would nullify those restrictions and revert to a 2020 framework that made the full 1.6 million acres of the Coastal Plain available for oil and gas development.

industries.rationale: The bill directly expands the acreage available for oil and gas leasing and development in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
Environmental and conservation organizations have a direct stake in decisions affecting protected wildlife refuge lands and resource extraction policies.

plain.whatItDoes: This joint resolution would open public land for oil and gas leasing in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who buys fuel or heats a home. People who live near a mine, and people who work in one.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what fuel costs. Nothing has changed yet. Most bills never become law.

method.formula: score = Σ_industries ( donorShare(industry) × billWeight(industry) ), where billWeight = classifierConfidence / Σ classifierConfidence. Range 0–1, read as a weighted share of disclosed itemized money.

ordinary.text: They wrote this bill. Sponsoring a bill about your own district's industry is the ordinary case, not the odd one.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
